I couldn't write any notes on Jeremiah 5 this time. My first attempt to open the source pages was blocked: the tool said I had no tool calls left for this turn. A second try failed the same way. That means I haven't read a single page from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Precept Austin, NET Bible or any other approved site.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I have no sourced material, any verse-by-verse notes I wrote now would be my own recollection, with URLs that I hadn't checked. So I've left them out instead of giving you something that only looks researched.

These are the pages I was going to read first. Once tool access is available again, I can start with them:
- Enduring Word: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-5/
- Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/jeremiah-5-commentary
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/jeremiah/5.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/jeremiah/5.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/jeremiah/5.htm
- NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Jeremiah+5

After those, I'd search the tradition-specific sites (Wesley, Spurgeon, Ligonier, LCMS, New Advent and others) for verses that are likely to show real differences. Examples are vv. 10 and 18 ("do not make a full end," which raises questions about God keeping a remnant), v. 3 (refusing correction and repentance) and v. 31 (false prophets and a people who "love it so"). I'd only include a tradition's view where its own teachers' pages actually address it.

Send the request again in a new message and I'll go straight to these sources.
